title: Ex-Google Exec: How to Position Yourself Now Before the Next AI Phase (2026–2027) | Mo Gawdat
guestTitle: Former Chief Business Officer at Google X · Author of Scary Smart
aboutGuest: Mo Gawdat spent over 12 years at Google as Chief Business Officer at Google X, where he ran business innovations and strategy. He is the author of Scary Smart and a vocal tech insider warning about AI's imminent impact on jobs, economics, and society. Gawdat recently built an AI startup and actively advises entrepreneurs on positioning themselves for the coming technological disruption.
summary: Mo Gawdat, former Chief Business Officer at Google X, presents a framework called FACE RIPS to describe seven dimensions of disruption expected to peak in 2027. He warns that within 2-3 years, the job market will experience massive shifts, with 23-30% of new grad hiring already collapsed. Gawdat argues that AI represents the last human innovation, as machines are already building other AIs and making scientific discoveries that will eventually automate every job AI performs better than humans. This technological displacement threatens to fundamentally reshape capitalism, economics, and labor arbitrage as we know it. Beyond job displacement, Gawdat identifies accountability as the critical missing element enabling all other dimensions of disruption—from power concentration among tech oligarchs to the erosion of authentic human connection through AI-generated content. He advocates that entrepreneurs have a unique window of opportunity now, as AI development cycles have compressed from 4 years to 6 weeks, but success requires mastering specific skills and abandoning traditional forecasting strategies.
keyTakeaways: AI development has compressed dramatically—Marina built an AI startup in 6 weeks that would have taken 4 years in 2022, fundamentally changing entrepreneurship from a chess game (forecasting the future) to squash (rapid adaptation to present conditions)

FACE RIPS framework identifies seven dimensions of disruption peaking in 2027: Power & Freedom, Reality & Connection, Innovation & Economics, and critically, Accountability—the missing element enabling all other dimensions to destabilize simultaneously

Job market collapse is already underway with 23-30% decline in new graduate hiring, and within 2-3 years, 10-20-30% unemployment will hit certain sectors as AI automates tasks better than humans across all industries

Accountability crisis—influencers, tech leaders, and AI systems face zero consequences for advice or decisions affecting millions, creating a world where power concentrates among tech oligarchs while responsibility vanishes

Four skills that matter now: understanding AI capabilities, rapid learning/adaptation, human connection, and strategic positioning before 2026-2027, as the next 12-15 years will be transitional disruption before potential stabilization
